newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets January interest subsidy at 2.87 pct.
newsitem.headline: China sets January interest subsidy at 2.87 pct.

text.p: The People's Bank of China, or central bank, has set the January interest rate subsidy on bank deposits of three years or more at 2.87 percent, the China Securities newspaper said on Monday.
The subsidy is paid only on new deposits.
The rate is down from the 3.72 percent announced in December.
The subsidy, paid on fixed deposits as they fall due, has been made on top of normal interest rates in order to attract long-term deposits during a period of high inflation.
But China stopped paying the subsidy on new deposits as of April as inflation has been easing.
The subsidy was introduced in March 1994 and hit a record of 13.24 percent in December of last year.
